inputs.goal: add SSO login to the web app in the platform repo

research.research_brief: The objective is to implement Single Sign-On (SSO) authentication for the web application within the platform repository. This involves integrating an SSO provider (e.g., Okta, Azure AD, or Google Workspace) into the existing web app architecture, ensuring secure token handling, and updating authentication flows to support SSO while maintaining backward compatibility with legacy login mechanisms.
research.prior_art: Prior research includes studies on federated identity management, OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect protocols, and enterprise SSO deployment patterns. Existing implementations in similar platforms demonstrate the importance of centralized identity brokers and granular permission scopes to mitigate security risks associated with third-party authentication.

plan.plan: Implement SSO login in the web app by integrating an SSO provider (e.g., Okta) using OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect protocols, update authentication flows to support SSO while maintaining backward compatibility with legacy mechanisms, and ensure secure token handling and centralized identity broker configuration.
acceptance_criteria: SSO login functionality is verified via integration testing with the selected provider
Documentation updated to reflect new authentication flow and SSO configuration
Human sign-off obtained on release documentation

steps.details: Identify and decompose the primary objective into actionable sub-tasks including integration planning, authentication flow modification, token handling, and verification.
Evaluate and select an appropriate SSO provider (e.g., Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace) based on compatibility with existing architecture and security requirements.
Create detailed design documents for integrating the chosen SSO provider using OAuth 2.0/OpenID Connect protocols while maintaining legacy login mechanisms.
Set up centralized identity broker within the platform repository to manage authentication and authorization processes securely.
Build necessary components for SSO integration including redirect URIs, token exchange mechanisms, and session management.
Establish secure methods for issuing, validating, and revoking authentication tokens while ensuring data protection.
Modify existing login workflows to support both SSO and legacy authentication methods seamlessly.
Perform comprehensive testing of the SSO implementation including edge cases, security validation, and backward compatibility checks.
Revise technical documentation to reflect new authentication flow, configuration settings, and user instructions for SSO login.
Secure approval from relevant stakeholders on release documentation and implementation approach.
Compile all necessary artifacts, deployment guides, and verification checklists for production release.
